sections.heading: The 30-Second Story
bullets: Shenzhen power-electronics platform company (founded 2003, SZSE: 002851) built by Huawei Electric / Emerson Network Power alumni — chairman-founder Tong Yongsheng was VP at both

Six business groups: appliance electric controls (38% of revenue), power products (28.5%), EV & rail components (12%), industrial automation (9%), intelligent equipment/welding (6%), precision connection (5%)
FY2025: ¥9.40B revenue (+15%), ~40% overseas, 8,894 employees, R&D held at ~12% of revenue for a decade
The headline story: the only mainland-China power supplier NVIDIA named for GB200 NVL72 — betting the company on the AI data-center 800VDC power transition

sections.heading: AI Data-Center Power — the Core Story
bullets: Full grid-to-GPU chain: solid-state transformer (>98.5% efficient, 800VDC out) → 800V HVDC Sidecar (>1 MW/rack, for NVIDIA Kyber-class racks) → 33 kW & 110 kW power shelves (110 kW liquid-cooled, for GB300/Vera Rubin) → BBU/supercapacitor backup shelves → CRPS/M-CRPS PSUs (up to 5.5 kW Ruby-efficiency, >100 W/in³)
Member of NVIDIA's May 2025 800V HVDC ecosystem alliance (alongside Delta, Flex, Lite-On); showed co-developed 800VDC sidecar at OCP Global Summit Oct 2025
Market reality: Taiwanese vendors hold ~74% of server PSUs (Delta ~41% alone); Megmeet's wedge is moving first on the 800VDC architecture change, not price
Honesty check: company itself said AI-server orders were small-batch and immaterial through 2025; first volume deliveries began end-2025, domestic hyperscaler volume expected 2026
US footprint: Dallas, Texas power test lab opened June 2026 (360 kW, roadmap 1.5 MW); Thailand plant phase II funded for overseas supply

sections.heading: Numbers That Matter
bullets: FY2025: revenue ¥9.40B (+15%) but net profit ¥146M (−67%); ex-non-recurring only ¥26M (−93%); Q4 2025 was a net loss; operating cash flow negative for the first time (−¥139M)
Why profits collapsed: AI-power R&D spend, overseas base build-outs, appliance price wars, and FX losses (India ≈17% of revenue; INR/USD volatility)
Q1 2026 rebound: revenue ¥2.79B (+20%), all six segments growing, power products +67%
Segment gross margins tell the strategy: welding/equipment 38.5%, automation 28%, appliances/power ~22%, EV 15% (doubled revenue at the lowest margin), precision connection 5%

Capital: ¥2.66B placement completed Feb 2026 (star investor Ge Weidong subscribed); Hong Kong A+H listing filed June 2026; stock ran ~¥24 (2024) → ¥190 peak (Jun 2026) → sharp July 2026 correction (three limit-downs); H1 2026 results due ~Aug 27

sections.heading: Beyond AI — the Other Five Legs
bullets: Appliance controls (largest, declining −5%): inverter HVAC/heat-pump controllers + smart-bathroom units (Yihe Bathroom); customers include Xiaomi, Haier, Hisense; rivals Topband, H&T Intelligent
EV & rail (+109%): motor controllers, OBC/DC-DC (1M+ two-in-one units shipped 2025), thermal management, active suspension; customers Geely, BAIC, Leapmotor, Changan
Industrial automation (+40%): MV800/MV520 drives, M5 servos, MU-series PLCs; wind-pitch drives in batch supply
Welding (+31%, best margins): Artsen/Ehave2/Dex digital welders, robotic welding power (1,800-unit repeat order from Honglu Steel), new laser-welding line
Network power heritage: Ericsson, Cisco, Juniper, Arista among named customers — the credibility base for the server-power push

sections.heading: People to Know
bullets: Tong Yongsheng (童永胜) — founder, chairman & president; PhD NUAA, post-doc Zhejiang University; ex-VP Huawei Electric and Emerson Network Power; controls ~24% with spouse
Shen Chuchun (沈楚春) — CTO; ex-chief engineer at Huawei Electric primary power and Emerson DC-Global
Wang Tao (王涛) — CFO & board secretary; ex-Huawei Electric and Emerson finance
The pattern: the entire senior bench is Huawei Electric → Emerson Network Power power-supply lineage — the same lineage as much of China's power-electronics industry

sections.heading: Watch Items
bullets: H1 2026 report (~Aug 27) is the first hard evidence of whether AI-DC revenue is materializing — consensus expects a ~6x FY2026 profit rebound
800VDC/HVDC technology routes not fully settled industry-wide; volume adoption of 1MW racks projected from ~2027
Balance-sheet strain: inventory +32% and receivables +19% in Q1 2026; guarantee quota >¥6B; HK listing adds dilution
FX remains a swing factor (USD, INR) — hedging acknowledged as incomplete

flashcards.q: What are Megmeet's six business groups, roughly by size?
flashcards.a: Smart appliance electric controls (~38% of FY2025 revenue), power products (~28.5%), new energy vehicle & rail components (~12%), industrial automation (~9%), intelligent equipment/welding (~6%), precision connection (~5%).

flashcards.q: What makes Megmeet notable in the NVIDIA ecosystem?
flashcards.a: It's the only mainland-China power supplier NVIDIA named for GB200 NVL72 power (Oct 2024), and a member of NVIDIA's 800V HVDC ecosystem alliance (May 2025) — supplying power shelves and pioneering the 800VDC sidecar architecture.
Revenue ¥9.40B (+15.1%); attributable net profit ¥146M (−66.6%); ex-non-recurring ¥26M (−93%); first negative operating cash flow (−¥139M); ~40% of revenue overseas.

flashcards.q: Why did profit collapse in FY2025 despite growing revenue?
flashcards.a: Heavy R&D on AI data-center power, overseas base build-out costs (Thailand, US, Hangzhou), appliance-sector price wars compressing gross margin (−2.9pp to 22.3%), and large FX losses (USD/INR).
An external 480/380VAC→800VDC power cabinet delivering >1 MW per rack for NVIDIA Kyber-class dense racks — Megmeet claims up to +5% end-to-end efficiency and −45% copper vs legacy in-rack AC power.

flashcards.q: What's Megmeet's flagship server PSU spec?
flashcards.a: CRPS/M-CRPS family from 800 W to 5.5 kW; the Ruby-efficiency M-CRPS 5.5 kW (launched Mar 2026) with power density >100 W/in³ — roughly double traditional PSU density.

flashcards.q: Who founded Megmeet and what's his background?
flashcards.a: Tong Yongsheng (童永胜), 2003. PhD from Nanjing University of Aeronautics & Astronautics, power-electronics post-doc at Zhejiang University; VP at Shenzhen Huawei Electric (1996–2001), then VP at Emerson Network Power (2001–2005).

flashcards.q: Who dominates the server power supply market Megmeet is attacking?
flashcards.a: Taiwanese suppliers hold ~74% — Delta Electronics alone ~41%, plus Lite-On, AcBel, Chicony, Advanced Energy. Trade press reports Megmeet displacing Lite-On as the #2 NVIDIA power-shelf source behind Delta (unconfirmed by the company).

flashcards.q: Which appliance-brand customers does Megmeet name?
flashcards.a: Xiaomi, Haier, Hisense, Changhong, Skyworth — plus the smart-bathroom business through subsidiary Yihe Bathroom.

flashcards.q: Which EV customers does Megmeet name, and what did it ship 1M+ of in 2025?
flashcards.a: Geely, BAIC New Energy, Leapmotor, Changan, Dongfeng, FAW; it shipped over 1 million two-in-one OBC+DC-DC onboard power units in 2025.

flashcards.q: What happened to Megmeet's stock in 2025–2026?
flashcards.a: Rode the AI-power narrative from ~¥24 (early 2024) to a ¥190 intraday peak / ~¥94.7B market cap (June 3, 2026), then crashed ~31% in 20 days in July 2026 with three 10% limit-downs; filed for a Hong Kong A+H listing June 29, 2026.

flashcards.q: What's the single most important upcoming event for the company?
flashcards.a: The H1 2026 report (~Aug 27, 2026) — the first hard test of whether AI data-center power revenue is actually ramping; consensus embeds a ~6x FY2026 profit rebound.

flashcards.q: Where does Megmeet manufacture and test outside mainland China?
flashcards.a: Thailand own-build plant (phase II funded), India local delivery, Germany and US presence — including a Dallas, Texas AI data-center power test lab opened June 2026 (360 kW, roadmap to 1.5 MW).

flashcards.q: What are Megmeet's welding flagships and its notable order win?
flashcards.a: Artsen/Artsen Plus, Ehave2 CM, and Dex digital inverter welders plus the SMARC IoT welding cloud; repeat strategic orders from Honglu Steel Construction — 1,500 robot-welding power sources (2024) + 1,800 more (May 2025).
